findings.message: the pattern matches 12 of 13 sample lines. It must match every one: a line it misses is dropped entirely, not partly parsed. The first it misses is 'Connection closed by 172.21.0.3 port 58450'. Of the 4 patterns, the closest to it is '^%{WORD:outcome} %{WORD:method} for (?:invalid user )?%{NOTSPACE:user} from %{IP:src_ip} port %{INT:src_port} ssh2$'. the pattern matches up to %{NOTSPACE:user}, which fails on 'by 172.21.0.3 port 58450'. %{WORD} matches letters, digits and underscore only - NOT a dot, hyphen, colon or slash. For a hostname use %{HOSTNAME}, for any run of non-space characters use %{NOTSPACE} If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.

findings.message: the extraction produced keys on 0 of 10 sample line(s). none of the patterns matches any sample line. The capture before it, %{LOGLEVEL:level}, matched only 'info' and stopped at '] tag: AUTHZ' - it is too narrow, and that is the one to widen. That position does not hold a bare number. Until this is right, every field is empty however it is mapped.
